title: Tenant-aware regional routing prioritizer with exemptions and model-variant fallbacks
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Background: Customers require deterministic routing that honors contract-level controls (e.g., EU-only data residency, enterprise tenant allowlists/denylists, and paid-tier priority). Current router returns a single chosen endpoint based primarily on region+capacity which makes it hard to reason about fallbacks and tenant exemptions. This ticket designs and implements a small policy service (Regional Prioritizer) that returns an explicit, ordered candidate list of routing targets with metadata and a deterministic routing signature that downstream gateways can use for enforcement and auditing.

Problem statement: We need a single source of truth that encodes: 1) tenant-specific residency constraints (eu_only, us_blocked), 2) tiered routing preferences (enterprise -> reserved -> hosted), 3) allow/deny overrides for specific customers, and 4) an ordered set of fallback model variants (e.g., float32->int8-quant->cpu-ffn) so that the serving layer can gracefully degrade while preserving compliance.

Proposed solution (high level): Build a microservice `regional-prioritizer` that: - Accepts request context (tenant_id, contract_flags, user_region_hint, requested_model_family, latency_budget_ms) - Evaluates tenant policy (allowlist/denylist, residency flags) stored in tenant-policy-store (read-through cache) - Produces an ordered list of candidate endpoints; each candidate includes: endpoint_id, region, model_variant, tier (hosted/dedicated/private), estimated_p95_latency_ms, compliance_tags, and a deterministic signature hash for auditability - Exposes a stable decision API /v1/prioritize that returns JSON and a gRPC alternative for low-latency callers - Emits routing_decision events to the observability pipeline (trace + structured metric) for cost and compliance telemetry

Key behavioral rules: - If tenant has eu_only true, all candidates must be EU-region (no cross-border fallback) unless the tenant has explicit emergency_escape policy (requires audit/log and separate approval flow). - Allowlist entries can add non-default permitted regions per-tenant; denylists exclude endpoints regardless of capacity. - Tier routing: prefer tenant's reserved pool (dedicated) if available and healthy. If reserved is saturated, prefer the next tier based on tenant contract (enterprise customers get hosted-reserved hybrid before falling back to public-hosted). - Fallback model variants should be ordered by quality-preserving heuristics (same architecture > quantized > truncated-context > CPU-only CPU-optimized) and annotated with expected quality delta and token-cost estimate.

Data model example (example JSON shown as an illustrative text blob to be consumed by engineers, not the microservice schema):
{
  "tenant_id": "acct_12abc",
  "constraints": {"eu_only": true, "emergency_escape": false},
  "requested_model_family": "redwood-7b",
  "candidates": [
    {"endpoint": "dedicated-eu-1", "model_variant": "redwood-7b-f32", "tier": "dedicated", "est_p95_ms": 60, "compliance_tags": ["eu"]},
    {"endpoint": "hosted-eu-2", "model_variant": "redwood-7b-int8", "tier": "hosted", "est_p95_ms": 85, "compliance_tags": ["eu"]}
  ]
}

Non-goals: This ticket does not change the serving runtime routing logic beyond consuming the prioritized candidate list. We will not implement autoscaling policy changes here.

Trade-offs considered: - Single service vs. embedding policy in API gateway: service centralizes policy and is easier to audit and evolve but adds a network hop; mitigated by local caching and a gRPC fast-path. - Conservative compliance-first behavior may increase cost by restricting fallbacks; we introduce an 'emergency_escape' flag on contracts to allow costlier but necessary escapes with audit logs. - Full policy language vs. simple structured flags: start with structured flags + allowance lists to keep rollout low-friction; expand to policy DSL in later iteration.

Implementation sketch: - Phase 1 (MVP): read-only prioritizer service, tenant-policy-store read cache, REST + gRPC endpoints, decision trace logging, integration tests. - Phase 2: dynamic policy edit UI hooks (Console), canary rollout to 10% of tenants, SLO alerts, and rollout dashboard. - Phase 3: policy DSL, per-route evaluations, and integration with rollout engine for blackouts.

Operational concerns: - Deterministic signature must be stable across minor config changes to avoid noisy reroutes; signature algorithm documented in design doc. - Audit log retention and export for compliance teams. - Metrics: routing_decisions.total, routing_fallbacks.count, routing_violations.count, avg_est_p95_ms_by_tenant_tier.

comments: 2025-02-19 - Sync with PM (Sofia Clarke): Confirmed EU-only contract must never cross-border. PM requested a clear emergency_escape workflow for legal signoff.
2025-02-25 - Eng architecture review: Decided on read-through cache + local LRU to keep latency under 5ms for warm lookups. Marco to prototype signature hashing with HMAC-SHA256.
2025-02-28 - Design feedback (Lina Park): Add UI flags for tenant exemptions and an 'audit reason' text field when enabling emergency_escape.
2025-03-03 - Security review kickoff: need key-management plan for signing decision signatures and RBAC for policy editors. Security ticket TBD.
2025-03-04 - Implementation note: basic REST API and unit tests merged to feature branch. Integration tests with serving proxy mocked; observed 4ms median extra latency on cold cache.
acceptance_criteria: /v1/prioritize returns ordered candidate list and deterministic signature for provided tenant context
All tenants with eu_only=true only receive EU-region candidates unless emergency_escape=true and audit flag set
Routing decisions are emitted to observability pipeline with tenant_id, chosen_endpoint, and fallback_reason
E2E integration test demonstrates fallback from dedicated -> hosted int8 variant while preserving compliance tags
Security review completed and signing keys provisioned for decision signatures
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy evaluation (allowlist/denylist, residency flags, tier precedence)
Integration tests: end-to-end flow from API gateway -> prioritizer -> mock-serving that validates signature and candidate order
Canary rollout: ship to 5% of traffic, monitor routing_violations.count and latency SLOs for 48h
Chaos test: simulate dedicated pool outage and validate fallback ordering and metric emission
Compliance audit: generate sample audit logfile for three tenants (eu_only, enterprise with allowlist, emergency_escape true)
